I love setting up a space that feels cozy and comforting, like a little escape where creativity flows effortlessly. It’s not just about making art— it’s about feeling at home in the process, free to explore, express and just be. When the space feels right, the creativity just flows 💛
Love, like art, isn’t about perfection—it’s about expression, emotion, and the beauty found in every raw, honest moment. May your heart always find its canvas 🌈 happy valentines day 💘

‘Echoes of her Soul’ 🌊

There is a softness in her eyes, a depth that speaks of dreams unspoken and battles fought in silence. She knows what it means to stand at the edge of uncertainty, to be against all odds and yet, she does not break. She breathes, she feels, she moves forward—one step, one heartbeat, one moment at a time.

Fear may walk beside her, but it does not lead her. Instead, she listens to the whispers of her own soul, the quiet reminders that she is more than her hesitation, stronger than her worries 💌

And as she steps forward, fear fades into the background, becoming nothing more than a ripple in the vast ocean of her becoming 🌸

If fear sits beside you, if doubt whispers in your ear—remember this:
You don’t have to be fearless to be brave. You’re doing better than you think. 
Life got you! 💪❤️

Right now, your girl is making do with whatever corner of home she can find—no fixed space, just moving around, setting up, and packing away every time guests come 🫠

When I need to shoot content, I go to a different space, and when I just want to paint freely, without the pressure of recording, I find myself somewhere I can spill paint without a second thought.

It’s a constant shuffle, and honestly, it’s exhausting. I love what I do, but not having a space that’s truly mine makes everything feel temporary. It’s hard to get into a real creative flow when you’re always setting up and breaking down, never fully settling in.

I know so many creatives can relate to this—the dream of having a space that’s just for you, where your art can live and breathe without interruption. A place where you don’t have to clear things away at the end of the day, where you can leave a half-finished painting out without worrying about someone else needing the space.

So, here I am, putting it out into the universe—manifesting my own art studio in 2025. A place where I can paint, shoot, make a mess, and just create freely. I don’t know when or how, but I know it’s coming. And when it does, I’ll look back at these days and remind myself how far I’ve come 🌟

caption: where’s the lie 🫢🫠

And just like that, my 100-day challenge of posting daily comes to an end 🌈
Ending it on a high note with my favorite painting—one that truly speaks to my heart— Wishing Well 🦋

Thank you all for your endless love and support 💛

I never imagined I’d be working on such big canvases—what once felt like a distant dream is now a reality🥹

I started with abstract art, where colours flow freely, no rules, no pressure—just pure expression. Back then, I never thought I’d step into the world of realism and now, here I am, painting things I once believed were beyond my reach 

It’s a reminder that we don’t have to figure everything out all at once but if we just keep going, keep learning, and keep showing up, we may end up surprising ourselves. Growth happens in ways we don’t always see coming, and honestly, that’s the magic & beauty of time 🌟

✨SURRENDER✨

Let go, my love, don’t chase the tide, 🌊
The universe whispers, ‘I’m on your side’ 🪽
You don’t have to race, you don’t have to know,
Some things are meant to take time to grow 🌱

The stars don’t rush, yet they always shine, 🌟
The river flows, yet it takes its time 
So breathe, lean back, and trust the way, 
What’s meant for you will never stray 🌙

No need to force, no need to fight,
The dawn will come, just trust the night 🌠
Surrender, soften, let life be—
The universe is working, always, for thee 👼

Tu duaaon ka hai ghar ❤️

I always rush through meals, grabbing something quick before diving straight into work. I get so caught up that eating becomes an afterthought. But mom? She notices. She always does.

So here she is, making sure I eat—because she knows I won’t do it myself until I’m done working. She doesn’t ask, she doesn’t wait, she just puts food in front of me, knowing I need it before I even realize it myself 

It’s true what they say— A mother’s love knows no bounds 😇

I recently visited Neem Karoli Baba’s Ashram and experienced an energy too profound for words. That moment stayed with me, and I felt an undeniable pull to express it in the only way I could— art. 

This painting is more than just what meets the surface— it’s my way of channelling the divine presence I felt, a humble attempt to bring to life the peace, grace and love that Baba embodied. Every strike carries the peace and power I felt that day, and I hope you’re able to feel it too ❤️

It’s still a work in progress, but I couldn’t resist sharing this journey with you all 🌈

Stay tuned for the final reveal 🫶🏻

What do you think? Do we like the colour combo & composition?

After completing my MBA, I tried finding a job but nothing came through. Then, I got an interview offer in Dubai but it happened to be at the same time as my art exhibition. My mind told me to take the safe path, to think about the future, but my heart was clear—I didn’t want to miss even a single moment of my exhibition.

So, I skipped the interview & went on with the exhibition. I had just started with art at that time, and for some reason I never questioned whether it’s the right path for me (even when I had zero sale). I’m usually a huge overthinker, analyzing every little decision to death but with art, I just feel at home ❤️

I sometimes regret spending so much on college and wish I had invested that money building my own art studio. (Just the thought of it gets me so excited) But I believe everything happens in its own time. If things had been easier, maybe I wouldn’t have learned the true value of this journey 💫

Here’s a little wish I’m sending out into the universe—and I hope you’ll wish for me too: 

Manifesting my art studio in 2025 🧿

I can’t get over how beautiful this floral heart’s bouquet has turned out 😍

I’ve been experimenting with alcohol inks lately, and I’m honestly amazed at how versatile this medium is. Each time I try something new, it surprises me in the best way possible ❤️‍🔥 
The colors, the flow, the way they mix—there’s just something so magical about it ✨🪽

Next, I’m thinking of creating a word with a dreamy alcohol ink background. What do you think? Any fun ideas or words you’d love to see? Drop your suggestions 💬🌸

caption:
Wait for the end 💌 

A painting that speaks to me ⭐️

So, I started this painting 20 days ago, and initially I had no goal of finishing it before Janamashtami. But as the festival got closer, I suddenly felt the urge to complete it in time. Normally, it takes me a month to finish such works, but I don’t know how this determination came over me- I was hellbent on completing it before the big day 

There were moments when it felt impossible, but I kept pushing myself, making sure to work on it every day, no matter how I felt. I didn’t let my mood come in the way, even though it’s easy to put things off because of a creative block or ‘abhi mann nahi hai yaar’. This experience taught me that consistency is matters more than motivation! I hope I can keep this mindset in the future too 🤞

So, here I present- ‘The Playful Divine’ 
55 cm x 50 cm 
Oil Pastels on Pastel Sheet 

His playful spirit and pureness is something I really connect with, and I wanted to share that feeling through this piece. I hope this piece fills your heart with warmth, joy, and a sense of peace ✨
Happy Janamashtmi 🙏❤️

PS: the performance was impromptu 🤭 I wanted to unveil the painting in a creative way and combining my love for art and dance seemed the perfect choice ☺️ hope you like it 🫶🏻

As I approach my 27th birthday, I’ve been reflecting on the journey so far and the realisations I’ve had along the way. Here are some of them ✨🌸

1. It’s totally okay to be single and not have found your soulmate yet. Maybe the universe is giving you time to really figure out what you want, rather than rushing into anything just for the sake of it.

2. Feeling lost is something we all experience. Each day brings new emotions. You might feel uncertain one moment and incredibly happy the next. Emotions come and go like visitors; it’s important to observe them rather than let them overwhelm you.

3. Age is just a number and time a concept. People might pressure you, saying you’re late to certain milestones like marriage. Don’t let their expectations dictate your choices. They don’t know your journey, and sometimes you’re still figuring things out. Take time to understand yourself and your desires before making big decisions.

4. Loneliness can feel scary, but it’s not the worst thing. It’s better to be true to yourself than to try fitting in where you don’t belong. Embrace your own company and learn to enjoy your own space. At the end of the day, you’re the only one who truly understands you truly. 

5. Invest in yourself. Strive for financial independence, no matter your background. Earning your own money gives you the freedom to make decisions independently. Start small, but take those first steps toward personal and financial empowerment.
